description: Hand-written earlier session in this repository (synthetic: the requests, thoughts, and answers were written for receipts-bench; every tool output was captured by running the step on the starting repository).

episodes.request: How does the due line show the long form of a date, and how does it write the number of days in the status text? Just look, please, no changes.

steps.thought: Both pieces of text should be in src/report.ts.
Look at how the tests pin the text.

finish.report: The long form is longDate in src/report.ts: the day number, the three-letter month name, and the year, for example 5 Jan 2027 or 31 Dec 2027; dueLine puts it in brackets at the end of the due line, after the due date and its weekday. Day counts are written by daysText (also src/report.ts): the singular form when the absolute value is exactly 1 (1 day, -1 day) and the plural otherwise (0 days, 12 days, -3 days). It is used twice in src/status.ts for the overdue and due-in texts and once in src/cli.ts for the between output. test/report.test.ts has five tests, one for each of longDate, the two forms of dueLine, scheduleLine, and daysText.

episodes.request: How does the status command decide between overdue, due today, and due in N days? No changes.

steps.thought: The tests show the exact wording.

finish.thought: The function and its callers are clear.
finish.report: paymentStatus in src/status.ts compares the as-of date with the due date. Equal dates give due today; an as-of date after the due date gives overdue by N days (or 1 day); an earlier as-of date gives due in N days, with daysText choosing the singular for exactly one. The between command uses daysBetweenDates, which returns the day difference from the first date to the second, so it is negative when the second date is earlier. Both are called only from src/cli.ts (lines 65 and 69). test/status.test.ts pins the wording with four tests: open, due today, overdue, and the day count between two dates.
